one_month_reasoning: The main event likely inside the window is Q3 2026 earnings. Quanta has not announced the date yet (the IR calendar listed no events on 2026-10-02), but Q3 results came out on Oct 31, 2024 and Oct 30, 2025, so I put roughly 75% odds on a report by Oct 30, 2026. Quanta has beaten and raised every quarter in 2026: guidance went from $12.65-13.35 adj EPS in February to $16.45-16.95 in July, and Q2 adj EPS was $4.24 against about $3.31 consensus. Even so, the stock fell about 12% between June 30 and late September, so beats are not being paid for. I expect another beat and a narrow raise, plus early 2027 framing (NiSource program entering backlog, larger programs 'stacking' from H2 2027). That gives a small upward tilt, with a median of about $666 against $662.60. The earnings print widens the spread a little versus plain monthly vol (44%/3.5 = 12.6%), so I used about 13% one-month sigma. Short-term factors pull in both directions: there is negative momentum, but also a Sept 24 Bernstein upgrade and a bounce off about $622. I stay close to symmetric and do not make a confident directional call.

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (bridge NTM EPS at Oct-2027 of about $21.7 x 31x = $673, weight 0.5), FCF yield (2028E FCF $3.1B at a 3.0% yield over ~151M shares = $684, weight 0.25) and EV/EBITDA (NTM EBITDA ~$5.3B x 20x less ~$6.0B net debt over ~151M shares = $662, weight 0.25). Blended about $675.

inputs_detail.derivation: Yahoo consensus is $19.64 from 25 analysts. That is about +17.5% on the $16.70 guide midpoint and fits record 12-month backlog of $32.3B (Q2 revenue run-rate ~$38B) and acquisitions contributing a full year.

2027E grown about 15%, in line with the Street's ~15% long-run EPS CAGR (TIKR/Bernstein note). Investor Day 2030 targets (7-10% organic growth, up to 80bps EBITDA margin expansion, capital deployment at 1.5-2.0x leverage, $21.60-26.75 2030 EPS) are now clearly conservative given the 2026 guide of $16.70 versus $13.00 on Investor Day.

The stock trades at about 34x 2027 consensus today ($662.6/$19.64), and TIKR put it at ~35x forward on Sept 24. I trim to 31x because growth is likely to slow from ~55% in 2026 toward the mid-teens in 2028, while keeping a premium over the 25% 10-year adj EPS CAGR history and 12-15% ROIC targets.
2026 guide midpoint $4.15B grown about 15% a year for two years, in line with EPS growth and margins holding near 10.5% (Investor Day target band 10-11%).
$5.5B x ~56% conversion (between the 53% in 2026E and the 55-60% 2030 target).
FCF yield on 2026 guidance is about 2.3% at the current ~$100B market cap. I allow modest normalization toward 3% as growth decelerates, consistent with the P/E compression assumed above.
150.34M basic outstanding on 7/27/26 and 152.4M Q2 weighted diluted (2026 guide 152.5M). No buybacks in H1 2026 against a $1.0B authorization, offset by share-settled acquisitions, so roughly flat.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: NTM EBITDA at Oct-2027 ~$5.3B x 20x = $106B EV less ~$6.0B net debt / ~151M shares

inputs_detail.derivation: Blend of ~$4.8B 2027E and ~$5.5B 2028E, each built from the 2026 guide midpoint of $4.15B at about +15% a year.

Current EV is about $106B ($99.8B market cap plus ~$6.5B net debt), which is about 25.5x 2026E and 22x 2027E EBITDA. I assume about 2x of compression by Oct-2027 as growth slows, consistent with the P/E method.

Pro forma debt is about $7.0B after the Aug-2026 $2B notes (424B5), less ~$0.5B cash, so ~$6.5B now. Assume FCF of ~$2.7B over 12 months is mostly redeployed into M&A, as at the Investor Day 1.5-2.0x leverage target, leaving net debt modestly lower.

bear.story: AI/hyperscaler capex digestion or a power-policy shock slows large-load awards. Margins slip from the 11.5% Electric peak as labor costs and fixed-price risk bite, 2027 guidance comes in near +8-10% EPS growth (~$18.5), and the multiple derates toward ~23x. That gives about $430, near the 52-week low of $404.

base.story: 2027 adj EPS lands at about $19.6-20, NiSource and other large programs enter backlog in H2 2026 and ramp through 2027, Electric margins sit near 10.5-11%, and the forward multiple compresses to ~31-32x on ~$22 NTM EPS. That gives about $700.

bull.story: Another 2026-style beat-and-raise year: 2027 EPS ~$21+, 765kV transmission and gas generation awards stack ahead of schedule, management upgrades the 2030 targets (2026 already tracks well above the Investor Day path), and the multiple holds about 36x on ~$26 NTM EPS. That gives about $960.

thesis_break_reason: $430 is about 35% below today and roughly 22x 2027 consensus EPS. A move there would most likely mean the market sees a real break, not ordinary volatility at 44% vol: a cut to 2026/27 guidance, a backlog decline, a large fixed-price or project loss, or a hyperscaler capex pullback that removes the technology and load-center growth leg (guided +220-240% in 2026). It is also just above the 52-week low of $404.51.

NiSource power-generation and grid program RPO/backlog recognition as permits are obtained
Hyperscaler Q4 earnings and 2027 capex guides (large-load demand read-through)
Annual meeting; possible buyback use under the $1.0B authorization (none used in H1 2026)
Q2 2027 earnings; timing of the H2-2027 'stacking' of large programs management flagged
Silverado wildfire litigation (subsidiaries tendered defense by SCE); collection of remaining unapproved change orders ($411M at 6/30/26, down from $984M)

key_uncertainties: How durable AI/data-center capex is: technology and load centers is ~10-20% of revenue but the fastest-growing piece
Multiple: the stock is about 34x 2027 EPS, so a reversion toward the historical mid-20s would offset a year of growth
Margin sustainability: Electric 11.5% in Q2 against a 10.5-10.75% full-year guide and a 10.0-11.0% long-term target
Integrating heavy M&A ($1.24B upfront in Q2/July plus up to $242M earnouts) and labor scaling (~15k hires a year)
Timing of large programs (NiSource excluded from Q2 backlog; management points to H2 2027 for the field-work ramp)
Whether Q3 2026 earnings fall inside the 1-month window (date not yet announced)
reasoning: Most of the evidence comes from primary filings. The Q2-26 8-K and operational commentary show revenue +41% (27% organic), adj EPS $4.24 (+71%), record backlog of $53.4B ($32.3B over 12 months), and a FY26 guide raised to $16.45-16.95 adj EPS and $2.0-2.5B FCF. The 2026 Investor Day (Mar 31) set 2030 adj EPS at $21.60-26.75, which now looks conservative against the 2026 guide of $16.70 (it was $13.00 at Investor Day). The 10-Q shows no buybacks in H1 despite a new $1B authorization, share-settled M&A, and unapproved change orders falling from $984M to $411M, which reduces Canadian project claim risk. The 424B5 shows $2B of new notes, putting pro forma debt at about $7.0B, with leverage 1.72x against a 1.5-2.0x target. Consensus 2027 EPS is $19.64, so the stock is at about 34x. My blended fair value is about $675 (P/E, FCF yield and EV/EBITDA all land at $660-685). That is close to spot because I assume growth is largely offset by multiple compression as EPS growth decelerates from ~55% toward the mid-teens. The scenario-weighted value is about $705 (bear $430 at 22%, base $700 at 53%, bull $960 at 25%). For the ladder I used a lognormal with a median of about $680 and sigma about 0.41, slightly below the 44% realized vol because backlog visibility is high, then fattened the far left tail a little for AI-capex shock risk. That gives P(>= $663) ≈ 0.52 and roughly a 25% chance of >= $895 and of <= ~$520. Research leaned on filings and company documents. Sell-side and press were used only for the consensus EPS and multiple context, and Twelve Data estimates were unavailable on this plan.
